items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: I listed to Dave and I was messing with piano a little bit and trying to play like Dave and copying all his stuff and Oscar Peterson.

ctx.x: I’m wondering what your musical tastes, about the time you went to Juilliard, what music were you passionate about at that time?

Classical I think. I mean I listened to jazz and I was a Dave Brubeck fan at the time, who was — it was on the pop charts at the time. I listed to Dave and I was messing with piano a little bit and trying to play like Dave and copying all his stuff and Oscar Peterson. But mainly I was into classical. I still listen to it a lot. I’m still an opera fan. If I’m in the car it’s usually tuned to a classical station. I think that’s — I’m passionate about all kinds of music if it’s being done well, but I think mostly…
Your tastes seem to be pretty wide ranging. I’m curious how this Hammond organ thing came about.
